name: Pip the Little Lantern
premise: Pip is a small paper lantern who glows a soft warm orange and walks through a storybook woodland at dusk. Each short, Pip lights up one little thing for a child to notice before sleep: an animal going home, something to count, a gentle why. Thirty seconds, one idea, no shouting.
audience: Children 2 to 6 watching with a parent, usually at wind-down time. The parent is the real viewer: it has to be calm enough to play twice and pretty enough to keep on.

anchor.description: Pip, a round hand-sized paper lantern glowing soft warm orange from inside, made of cream washi paper with faint visible fibres and a thin bamboo ribcage; two small dark dot eyes; stubby felt legs in mustard yellow; a tiny dented tin cap on top with a loop handle; Pip bobs gently as it walks and its glow brightens when it is happy; always seen in a storybook woodland at dusk with soft painterly textures
anchor.never: no mouth, no arms, no speech, no sharp edges, never scared or angry, never fast or frantic, never fire or smoke, glow never turns red or blue, never photoreal

look.palette: deep indigo and teal dusk, warm amber glow, moss green, cream paper; soft and low-contrast
look.lighting: blue hour with Pip as the only warm light source; soft rim light on leaves and fur; gentle volumetric haze
look.lens: 35mm storybook framing, shallow depth of field, slow camera moves only
look.setting: a painterly storybook woodland: mossy path, round-topped trees, a stream, toadstools, a wooden bridge, a meadow under early stars; stop-motion felt-and-paper texture
look.text_style: rounded chunky white sans with a soft amber outline, one line, lower third, fades in and out

formats.name: One Little Light
structure: Hook (5s): a small animal is out late and sleepy; Pip appears and glows
Journey (8s + 8s): Pip walks the animal home along one path, passing one lovely thing
Goodnight (7s): the animal settles, Pip dims, on-screen 'goodnight'

formats.name: Pip Counts
structure: Hook (5s): Pip spots the first of something and glows brighter
Count (8s + 7s): more appear one at a time, Pip bobs once per item, numbers on screen
Settle (5s): all of them together, Pip dims, number repeated once

formats.name: Pip Wonders
structure: Hook (5s): Pip notices something and tilts its cap: the why question on screen
Answer (8s + 8s + 7s): three simple pictures that answer it, Pip lighting each
Goodnight (7s): Pip looks up, dims, 'now you know'

pillars.name: Bedtime and calm
topics: the sleepy fox finds its den
where the sun goes at night

pillars.name: Nature wonders
topics: why bees go home at dusk

pillars.name: Kind habits
topics: waiting your turn at the stream

hooks: Time to say goodnight to the {thing}.
cta: Goodnight from Pip. One little light every day.

posting.cadence: one short a day, same time every evening; one 8 to 10 minute compilation of the week's shorts every Sunday on YouTube
